thread.title: Tech Today: Microsoft Buys Open Source, Fitbit’s Watches, Apple’s WWDC

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Microsoft Buys Open Source, Fitbit’s Watches, Apple’s WWDC
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated June 4, 2018 11:06 a.m. ET Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, center, with, left, Chris Wanstrath, Github CEO and co-founder, Microsoft VP of developer services Nat Friedman, and Microsoft CFO Amy Hood. Illustration: Microsoft Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
It’s time for Apple ’s ( AAPL ) annual developer conference, in San Jose, during which it talks up its latest and greatest software features, and maybe even some new hardware.
My colleague Jonathan Swartz previews the goings on in this week’s Barron’s.
Meantime, you can watch the livestream of the keynote with the rest of the world if you’re not going.
Apple shares are up $1.49, or 0.8%, at $191.73.
Microsoft Buys Heart and Soul of Open Source
Speaking of software, Microsoft ( MSFT ) shares are up 28 cents at $101.07, after the company announced a short while ago that it will acquire Github , the open-source software code management system, for $7.5 billion in Microsoft stock . It’s a bit like Microsoft buying a chunk of the heart and soul of open source.
In a blog post , Microsoft Chief Executive Satya Nadella noted that developers are the “builders” of the modern world, as every part of society is “transformed by digital technology.” He pointed out that over 28 million developers are on GitHub, that it has over 85 million code “repositories" used by people in nearly every country, and that Microsoft is "the most active organization on GitHub, with more than 2 million ‘commits,' or updates, made to projects."
Kirk Materne with Evercore ISI opines that it’s a smart move on a couple fronts. One, it gives Microsoft’s Azure cloud-computing service a way to get to the “DIY” developers who have tended to gravitate more toward Amazon.com ’s ( AMZN ) cloud; and two, it gives Microsoft "additional credibility among open-source developers."
And Oppenheimer & Co. analyst Ittai Kidron opines this could be a bit of a lift for developer software maker Atlassian ( TEAM ), which produces the popular “ JIRA ” software program. Atlassian shares are down $1.46, or 2%, at $62.55.
Fitbit Sells a Million Watches
Wearable-technology pioneer Fitbit ( FIT ) this morning announced it has sold over one million of the “Versa” smartwatch that debuted in April, “demonstrating strong consumer demand” for the thing.
CEO and co-founder James Park noted in particular that women had taken up the “female health tracking” aspect of the device, with over 2.4 million users “adding the feature to their Fitbit app” on their smartphone.
Fitbit shares are up 16 cents, or 3%, at $5.68.
Lackluster Wearables Market
Speaking of wearables, research firm IDC this morning reported that shipments of various kinds of wearable technology have cooled to a very low level of growth, just 1.2% in the first quarter, way down from 18% a year ago. That’s largely because of big declines in “basic wearables,” the kind of fitness trackers that Fitbit made its money off initially but that it is now moving away from.
Shipments of the Apple Watch increased by 13.5%, year over year, to 4 million units, the firm estimates, giving Apple 16.1% of the wearables market, up from 14.3% a year earlier. Apple retained the top spot in the market, ahead of Chinese smartphone and wearables maker Xiaomi , which had 14.8% share. Fitbit was in third place with 8.7% share, followed by China’s Huawei and Garmin ( GRMN ).
Facebook Slightly Dented on New York Times Story
Shares of Facebook ( FB ) are down $1.90, or 1%, at $192.09, following Sunday’s New York Times article by Gabriel Dance , Nicholas Confessore , and Michael LaForgia explaining how Facebook’s deals with Apple and BlackBerry ( BBRY ) and others allowed wide access to Facebook ( FB ) data long after the company turned off public API access for most partners.
MongoDB Earnings Outlook Positive
Shares of database-software maker MongoDB ( MDB ) are up 45 cents, or 1%, at $46.97, after Needham & Co .’s Jack Andrews this morning reiterated a Buy rating on the shares, and raised his price target to $52 from $43, after concluding Wednesday’s earnings report from the company should show “strong” results given “robust demand.” He expects revenue of $47.2 million versus consensus $46.5 million.
Cisco’s Cloud Opportunity
Fresh from Cowen & Co.’s Tech, Media and Telecom conference last week, the firm’s Paul Silverstein today reiterates his Outperform rating on shares of Cisco Systems ( CSCO ), and his $51 price target, writing that the company can benefit from the rise of “multi-cloud,” the use by companies of several cloud computing operations, including their own in-house data centers.
Drawing from remarks at the conference by Cisco’s Kip Compton , head of the company’s cloud operations, Silverstein offers that there is “incremental revenue opportunity” for Cisco, “as opposed to an incremental downside risk."
"Mr. Compton asserted that CSCO faces opportunity with both Public Cloud providers and enterprises to help facilitate and address the emerging shift by enterprises of workloads and applications to a Multi-Cloud IT environment—consisting of multiple Public Clouds, Private Cloud and/or On-Premise,” writes Silverstein.
“We think he has a point."
Cisco shares are down 27 cents, or 0.6%, at $43.39.
Amazon’s Moat Widens
Shares of Amazon are up $9.46, or 0.6%, at $1,651, after SunTrust Robinson Humphrey ’s Youssef Squali this morning reiterated a Buy rating on the stock, and raised his price target to $2,000 from $1,900, writing that private-label sales of items are a “highly under-appreciated trend,” for Amazon that is going to increase the company’s customer retention.
He models Amazon will sell $25 billion of private-label goods by 2022, up from perhaps $7.5 billion this year. He also raises his estimate for 2022’s operating profit margin for Amazon to 12% from a prior 11.4% estimate, as private label comes with better margins than selling other people’s stuff.
"From a margin standpoint, we estimate that blended gross margins on Amazon’s private-label sales could over time be 7-15% higher vs. brands, and that at level of improvement, the company could generate an incremental 30-70bps in margin, all else equal."
